lecture_summary: The lecture develops sinusoidal traveling-wave mathematics, distinguishes propagation speed from particle motion, applies string-wave speed to a hanging-mass system, uses spherical wavefront geometry, examines refractive index and wavelength changes across media, and concludes with wave power, inverse-square intensity, and decibels.

videos.title: Wave Speed on a String - Tension Force, Intensity, Power, Amplitude, Frequency - Inverse Square Law
videos.reason: Best anchor video: covers string tension and linear density, wave-speed/frequency/wavelength relationships, amplitude and power, and inverse-square intensity. It addresses the lecture’s largest mechanical-wave and intensity clusters without requiring separate overlapping videos.

videos.title: Snell's Law & Index of Refraction Practice Problems - Physics
videos.reason: Strongest optics match because it applies refractive index to light speed and wavelength in different materials, supporting the lecture’s medium comparisons and wavelength-in-glass calculations.

videos.title: Sound Intensity Level in Decibels & Distance - Physics Problems
videos.reason: Adds the distinct logarithmic skill missing from the first video: converting between intensity and decibels and determining how sound level changes with distance.
